response.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT st.healtheval AS h, AVG(sc.gbsize / NULLIF(sc.spanmin, 0)) AS rate, COUNT(sc.gbsize / NULLIF(sc.spanmin, 0)) AS cnt FROM scans sc JOIN sites st ON sc.zoneref = st.zoneregistry GROUP BY st.healtheval), o AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS a FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.rate) AS avg_rate, AVG(r.cnt * 1.0) AS avg_count, AVG(r.rate - o.a) AS avg_excess FROM r CROSS JOIN o WHERE r.rate > o.a

assumptions.assumption: A status's rate is the mean of per-scan gbsize/spanmin. Scans with a NULL gbsize or NULL/zero spanmin are ignored; zero spanmin is treated as missing to avoid division by zero.
The all-status average is the unweighted mean of the per-status average rates, not the mean over all scans.
The 'count' for a status is the number of its scans with a valid rate. Scans without one are not counted.
A NULL healtheval, if present, forms its own group, since the request says to group by that column.

alternatives.interpretation: The all-status average is the mean rate over all matched scans, so statuses with more scans weigh more.
